kinds.doc:
Knows one program: where its copies are, what is newest, and how to install it into a folder the host owns.

Every method is synchronous and required, and answers for the store as configured. Every object a method is handed is
the store's from then on, and it destroys each, even when it refuses. `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` always comes with the
reason.
kinds.name: program_store

slots.doc: Who the program is and where it is fetched from, with nothing run and no connection opened. The same on every call.
slots.name: describe

slots.doc:
The copies of the program it can find. With `probe` false it spawns nothing and answers from the managed copy and
`tools.find` alone; with it true it may run each copy's version flag through `spawner`, within
[`PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`]. It opens no network connection.
slots.name: program

slots.doc: The newest version on a channel, through `tools.fetch_text` only. A failure is `known: false` with the reason.
slots.name: latest

slots.doc:
What `apply` would do, before anything is written, with every change outside the host's folder. An update to the
version already current is a plan with nothing in it, never a refusal. A version the publisher no longer serves is
`GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` with the reason.
slots.name: plan

slots.doc:
Carries out the plan the person confirmed in `request.staging` and nowhere else. `spawner`'s private directory is
`request.staging`. It reads the version back by running the staged program, never from an installer's exit status. A
fact the plan rests on that has moved is `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` with `plan changed`.

When the person cancels (`prompter.cancelled()`, or a call answering `GUATIAO_ERR_GONE`) or `timeout_ms` passes, it
kills its whole process tree and answers `GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` within two seconds. It never switches versions: the host
does.
slots.name: apply

kinds.doc:
How an install tells the person what it is doing. The host implements it and hands one to
[`apply`](ProgramStore::apply); the store destroys it when the apply ends.

When the person cancels, every call answers `GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` and `cancelled` is true.
kinds.name: install_prompter

slots.doc: One line of output, as the program printed it.
slots.name: say

slots.doc: How far a download or a step has got.
slots.name: progress

slots.doc: The rare question, as a login asks one.
slots.name: ask

slots.doc: Whether the person cancelled.
slots.name: cancelled

kinds.doc:
What the host does for a store on the machine its spawner runs on: the checked fetch, the safe unpack and the look for
files. A store never opens a connection or writes a file by itself.
kinds.name: install_tools

slots.doc:
The files named in the request that exist, in the order the `PATH` and then `dirs` list them. Only absolute `PATH`
entries are read: never `.` and never a relative entry.
slots.name: find

slots.doc: A small text document: a version file, a manifest. `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for one over `max_bytes`.
slots.name: fetch_text

slots.doc:
A file into the granted folder, checked as it is written. A mismatch deletes it and answers
`GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` with `checksum mismatch`. The executable bit is set only after the check passes.
slots.name: fetch

slots.doc:
An archive inside the granted folder, unpacked. It refuses absolute paths, `..`, links, device names and anything
over its limits.
slots.name: unpack

kinds.doc:
Starts programs where the host chooses: on this machine, on another over SSH, in a container or
a virtual machine. The host implements it and hands one to every
[`AcpHarness::start`](crate::AcpHarness::start); the provider owns it from then on, starts its
programs through it, or never calls it, and destroys it by the time it calls the sink's
`closed`.

Every slot takes `&self`, so a provider may call it from several threads at once.
kinds.name: process_spawner

slots.doc: Where its programs run and what it can give them; the same on every call.
slots.name: describe

slots.doc:
Starts `spec` and hands over the process. Refuses `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` a spec asking
what [`describe`](Self::describe) says it cannot give, `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` a program
that is not there, `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` a spec it cannot read.
slots.name: spawn

slots.doc:
Writes `bytes` to the file `path` in the private directory the host granted this spawner (an
account's `state_dir`, or a login's), making directories on the way and replacing a file
there; `private` makes it readable by its owner alone where the system has such a notion.

**The host resolves every path** against that directory and never trusts the provider's:
`path` is relative, and an absolute path, a `..` part, or a link leading out of the directory
is `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND`, as is any call on a spawner with no such directory. A file
with another name for the same data (a hard link) is `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` too, where the
system lets the host see it. `private` is honoured where the file is made: on Unix the file
is created owner-only (mode 0600) before it holds a byte; on Windows the granted
directory's ACL is the guard. A spawner that cannot give files says `files` false in [`describe`](Self::describe) and refuses all four
file methods `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED`.
slots.name: write_file

slots.doc:
The content of the file `path`, whole. `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for a file that is not there
or a path [`write_file`](Self::write_file) refuses; `GUATIAO_ERR_BAD_VALUE` for one longer
than `max_bytes`, or a file that is not a regular file `GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND`.
slots.name: read_file

slots.doc:
How long the file `path` is and when it last changed; `None` when it is not there.
`GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for a path [`write_file`](Self::write_file) refuses.
slots.name: file_info

slots.doc:
Removes the file `path`; removing a file that is not there is no error.
`GUATIAO_ERR_NOT_FOUND` for a path [`write_file`](Self::write_file) refuses.
slots.name: remove_file

slots.doc:
Tells the host something about the connection this spawner serves that is no message of the
client's: the harness exited, gave a notice (a version it was not tested with), or a part of
the provider's own plumbing failed. The host logs it. Called from a thread of the provider's,
at any time while the connection runs, and never with client text or a value of the
environment or the credentials; a spawner that has no use for it returns `Ok`, and the
provider ignores a failure.
slots.name: notice

kinds.doc:
One program a spawner started, and everything it starts in turn.

Every slot takes `&self`, so one thread may write or kill while another waits in `read`.
Destroying it kills the whole tree, as [`kill`](Self::kill) does.
kinds.name: spawned_process

slots.doc:
Writes all of `bytes` to its standard input (its terminal's, with a terminal).
`GUATIAO_ERR_GONE` once the input is closed or the process has ended.
slots.name: write

slots.doc: Closes its standard input: the program reads the end. Closing it twice is no error.
slots.name: close_input

slots.doc:
Copies standard output (a terminal's whole output, with one) into `dst`: the byte count;
`0` once no more can ever come; [`READ_TIMED_OUT`] after `timeout_ms` with nothing (`0`
polls); [`READ_LINK_DOWN`] while the link is down. Never skips or repeats a byte, a link
that dropped and came back included.
slots.name: read

slots.doc:
The same for standard error, when the spec kept it [`ErrorOutput::Separate`]; `0` at once
otherwise.
slots.name: read_error

slots.doc: Resizes its terminal. `GUATIAO_ERR_UNSUPPORTED` for a process started without one.
slots.name: resize

slots.doc: Waits up to `timeout_ms` (`0` polls) for it to end, and answers how it stands.
slots.name: wait

slots.doc:
Ends it and every process it started: its process group or job, and those that left it
when [`SpawnerInfo::kills_escaped`] says so. Killing an ended process is no error.
slots.name: kill

slots.doc: Whether the link to where it runs is up, and how often it has dropped.
slots.name: link
